title: redis-cli: use CLIENT NO-TOUCH for key size analysis
body:
`redis-cli --bigkeys` and `--keystats` issue commands that perform read lookups. On LRU or LFU eviction policies, scanning can therefore make keys appear recently used or more frequently used.

To avoid this issue, we can enable `CLIENT NO-TOUCH ON` for `--bigkeys`, `--memkeys`, and `--keystats`. `--memkeys` does not currently touch LRU/LFU metadata, but enabling the mode keeps the key-size analysis commands consistent.

`CLIENT NO-TOUCH` is available since Redis 7.2. When it is unavailable or denied by ACLs, redis-cli continues with its existing behavior. I/O failures remain fatal.

`--scan` does not read key values, and `--hotkeys` uses `OBJECT FREQ`, which already performs a no-touch lookup, so neither mode needs this setting.

Mixed models from OpenAI were used.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CLI-only behavior with graceful fallback when NO-TOUCH is unsupported; covered by new integration tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Key-size analysis modes (`--bigkeys`, `--memkeys`, `--keystats`) now send **`CLIENT NO-TOUCH ON`** before the SCAN loop (alongside the existing cluster **`READONLY`** setup), so read lookups during inspection do not bump LRU idle time or LFU frequency on eviction-enabled instances.
> 
> The helper mirrors **`sendReadOnly`**: only I/O failures abort; error replies are ignored so older servers or ACL users without **`CLIENT`** still run the scan unchanged. Integration tests assert idletime/freq stay stable across those modes and that **`--keystats`** still completes when **`CLIENT`** is denied.
